pillarForecast.why: Turn 2.3 -> 1.8 is his own fix and big enough to feel; expect it to be absorbed silently, showing up as 'shook one into a rock' moments rather than as a comment about turning.

pillarForecast.pillar: Pursuers are the star / reference moment 2
pillarForecast.why: Both variants keep pursuers on screen ~55-68%; in A a tail behind him is literally the TIE-fighter picture and the most likely source of his best moment of the session.

A sends pursuers almost twice as often and allows 5 alive from sector 1, plus 1.35x catch-up when far: the tail never thins out, which can read as 'can't shake em' again or 'too many', in A specifically.
Warnings unchanged and praised; the wall knock-back removes the 'never got free' double hit silently. Small residual risk in A of a hit from behind while he looks ahead.

pillarForecast.pillar: P9 / P3 (runs build over minutes; run 5 looks different)
pillarForecast.why: Bots still reach ~2 under thrusters, so he likely stalls in sectors 2-3 from sector 1 for the 10th-15th run in a row; v9 already produced the first 'meh'. Expect fatigue and a progression proposal late in the session.
With pursuers weakened, the cost he raised in v9 shrinks; expect silence about controls again.

biggestRisk: Sector fatigue, not the A/B: the pursuer fixes make the dodging feel better, but bots under thrusters still reach only ~sector 2, so he is likely to keep dying in the Asteroid belt/Crossfire from sector 1 for the 10th-15th straight run. v9 ended on 'meh' after nine such runs; by runs 44-45 expect 'meh' and a request about progression (start from a checkpoint, see something new). A's doubled, catch-up-boosted swarm can add 'too many of them / can't shake em' and accelerate it.
abVerdict: Unlike past A/Bs, this one is visible and is his own complaint, so ~55% he names it in his words ('they're on my tail now', 'they came from the sides again'). He'll prefer A (~60%), framed as the TIE-fighter fantasy and being able to plan, with the main hedge being the number of pursuers in A ('a lot of them'); ~25% a third option such as 'from behind, but fewer' or 'mostly behind with the occasional flanker'. Sector reached will be about equal.
